node-1.label: Excessive sweating of the buttocks, most severe at the intergluteal cleft and sacrum

node-2.label: 31-year-old male nursing student with a history of axillary hyperhidrosis; axillary condition was previously treated successfully with 20% aluminum chloride, but aluminum chloride treatment for the intergluteal cleft and sacrum was unsuccessful

node-3.label: Due to severity of sweating, he used absorbent pads yet continued to soak through his pants and was unable to attend work

node-4.label: Physical examination with Minor starch-iodine test identified significant sweating areas in the sacral region (10 × 3 cm) and intergluteal cleft (6 × 8 cm)

why.why: Expert analysis supports primary focal hyperhidrosis based on localized sacral/intergluteal sweating, positive Minor starch-iodine test, prior axillary hyperhidrosis, and functional impairment. However, key diagnostic criteria (onset, family history, negative secondary screening, symmetry, sleep cessation) remain unverified, so the diagnosis is probable but not definitive; confidence is reduced from 0.75 to 0.70.

The absence of diffuse sweating and the localized pattern, reinforced by expert analysis stating secondary causes are unlikely, further refute a systemic cause. Confidence is lowered from 0.15 to 0.10.
Expert analysis considers compensatory hyperhidrosis unlikely given the focal pattern, and the clinical picture better aligns with a primary focal process; confidence is reduced from 0.10 to 0.08.
